baseline_prompt_en: Make an environmental self-portrait of a woman with reference-guided facial appearance, catching a self-authored portrait moment in a narrow working greenhouse. Use the supplied image as guidance for her face and hair: softly rounded facial proportions, a short straight dark bob and wispy bangs. The greenhouse has weathered green glazing bars, damp fern leaves and a waist-high wooden potting bench; a low roof joint above the screen-right end of the bench is still dripping after rain. She is protecting a creased paper seed envelope from the leak with a small, improvised arrangement, and the caught water makes her success visible. She stands behind the bench, weight settled evenly, torso inclined only slightly forward, elbows comfortably bent beside her torso. Her anatomical right hand, on screen-left, steadies the seed envelope on the flat base of an inverted terracotta bowl at the dry end of the bench. Her anatomical left hand, on screen-right, supports the middle of a narrow open brass half-channel at waist height. The channel slopes down to screen-right, its upper end directly under the roof drip and its lower open end above a zinc pail resting on a low wooden crate beside the bench. Bright droplets strike the upper trough, run along its concave interior and fall from its lower lip into the pail. A few pale seeds rest beside the open envelope on the dry clay surface. Both hand contacts and the water route are clearly visible. She has just lifted her attention toward the lens, her mouth holding a slight, lopsided smile of amused relief; her warm, direct eyes and relaxed shoulders make the portrait feel personal. She wears a faded olive canvas apron over a soft pale-green cotton blouse with rolled sleeves. The capture camera is secured on a dry shelf across the bench, facing her directly at eye level; a comfortable environmental frame from above her head to her knees includes both hands, the bowl, the full short channel and the receiving pail. Soft cool dawn through wet glass meets a gentle warmer patch on her face. Keep the facial presence primary, then let the two hand roles and the redirected water reveal why this quiet moment matters. Natural photographic textures, clear spatial depth, restrained color and lifelike skin.
